Patient: I'm 20 years old, and I'm female. I'm here for my yearly follow-up for asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy.
Doctor: Thank you for providing your age and gender. Could you please tell me more about the reason for your visit and any specific concerns you have during your yearly follow-up?
Patient: Sure, I'm here for my yearly check-up to make sure my asthma, allergies, and food allergy are all under control. I’ve been using Wixela since my insurance changed, and I also take Zyrtec for my seasonal allergies. I’m also working on reducing my inhaler use because I’m trying to join the military and need to show I can handle physical activity without it.
Doctor: Could you please describe your current asthma symptoms, including frequency and severity of wheezing, shortness of breath, or coughing, and whether you have experienced any exacerbations in the past year?
Patient: I haven't had any wheezing or shortness of breath, and my coughing is pretty minimal. I only use my albuterol inhaler rarely, usually before a workout or strenuous activity. I haven't had any asthma exacerbations in the past year.
Doctor: Can you provide details about your food allergy, including the specific food(s) you are allergic to, the severity of your reactions, and any management strategies you use?
Patient: I'm allergic to peanuts, and I had a reaction with hives when I touched peanuts in a car I was cleaning. Since then, I've been more cautious, like wearing long sleeves and changing gloves often. I also carry an epipen just in case. I avoid tree nuts too, even though I can tolerate almonds and cashews, I usually stay away from them if I can.
